YouTube Fan Finder and Insights Tutorial - Duration: 5 minutes, 56 seconds.<|endoftext|>GTN are going to be bringing you a series of videos to help you train and prepare for your first triathlon! You’ve entered your first event...but where do you start?
As a minimum, we would recommend 12 weeks to realistically prepare for, and complete a triathlon. That’s not to say that it’s not possible in less time, but to turn up feeling relaxed and confident, then this length of preparation should do the trick. So, we’ll be gearing our series of videos to a 10-12 week training time.
As triathletes, you have 3 sports to juggle and this can be quite challenging. If you work out six times in a week, you might swim twice, bike twice, and run twice, but your longest bike ride might be one hour, whereas your swims might last 30 minutes each and your runs, 40 minutes.
If you have a background in swimming, you can probably get away with doing a little less on your stronger discipline, and spend a little more time on your weaker disciplines. At least to bring them up to a point that you’re more comfortable with them. You can of course play to your strengths, but that’s for a later date, for now we want to make sure you complete your first triathlon comfortably.
Whilst training for your first triathlon, it’s mostly about completion. So following a gradual and sensible plan that keeps you consistent with your training is the key.
We like to explain it as if you’re building the foundations. You can’t move on without those foundations, otherwise it will all fall apart. So, whilst it’s tempting, the harder and faster stuff could be more detrimental if you do it before you’re ready to.
We’ve got three sports. That means three different sports to buy kit for. But, unless you really want to, there is no need to take out a mortgage for a new bike and other kit for your first triathlon. We’re sure you’ll love the sport, but until you’ve done an event it’s worth holding off on spending a load.
If you found this video useful, don't forget to give it a thumbs up and share with your friends!

VS Code...Maybe you've heard about it, or you've seen your friends using it... Maybe you've tried it once or twice, or maybe you use it every single day. No matter what camp you fall into, in this session you'll learn something new about using VS Code and how to quickly build and deploy node.js applications and micro-services.
We'll configure VS Code for the "inner loop" of development - the edit, compile, debug cycle. See how VS Code provides great code editing and code navigation experiences such as semantic IntelliSense, GoTo Definition, Find All References, Linting (e.g. ESLint), and more. We will configure VS Code to enable single file debugging, gulp file debugging, mocha debugging, and both client and server side debugging in a single session. You will see how easy it is to create Docker artifacts with VS Code, how to build and deploy images, and even how to debug your node.js applications running in containers.
All of this from within a lightweight editor, in under 30 minutes!
Chris Dias is a Program Manager, Microsoft. Chris is a member of the VS Code team at Microsoft, where he gets to work with an incredible group of engineers who are passionate about developer tools and changing the way Microsoft does development

Experience an eco nature resort on the Northwest Sri Lankan coast at its best. A place to feel home and immerse yourself in nature. A resort that is based in the jungle area of the Kappalady lagoon located right at the beach. Surrounded by tall coconut trees and lush greenery, Elements is a true haven to sit back, relax and let go. With the lagoon and the beach at just a stone's throw away, it offers to be the perfect location for kitesurfing, standup paddling (SUP) adventures and makes it a fantastic starting point for dolphin and whale watching. ​ Sitting in the lounge of your lagoon villa you may just wait and let the various rare water birds like king fishers, sea eagles and waders pass or fly by. ​ We have built our villas and bungalows with 100% indigenous materials mainly coconut leaves, wood and concrete. We use the cooling effect of the persistent wind to cool our bungalows with a clever and efficient ventilation and insulation system - thus not requiring A/C we manage to "be green" and contribute to the reduction of your carbon footprint during your holiday.

According to the Brazilian Federal Law 8.069/1990 minors under 18 years of age cannot check into hotels unless they are accompanied by their parents or a designated adult. Each coaster is made of a natural tumbled stone tile that is porous enough to absorb moisture from a cold beverage glass and maintain a lower temperature that helps keep your drink cold. There is no sealant applied for that reason. The unique characteristics of this type of material are not only beautiful, but amazingly practical and provide great protection for your valuable furnishings. All edges are hand sanded for a smooth touch. The natural beauty of the surface itself varies from stone to stone. The images applied are the only repetitive feature of each coaster. A set of four coasters will have as much similarity as possible while also keeping with the look of natural stone. The unique pits, edge variations (due to the tumbling process), and general coloration will play into the final appearance of the product in a way that cannot be matched by ceramic or resin based products. The images are chosen specifically to incorporate with the variations of tumbled marble and result in a very “pleasing to the eye” piece of décor with superior functionality. All coasters are made using a high quality, solvent ink that is permanent in the stone…meaning that it will not wash off. Water will not damage the design. All items that use ink will fade over time (i.e.: fabric, photos, etc), so be mindful of where you will be placing them…preferably indoors or away from intense sunlight.
All coasters are free of sealant to assure maximum absorption of condensation. We can apply a protective layer of sealant FREE of charge. It will not change the appearance of the coaster in any way. This can be done by entering in the word “SEALANT” in the comment box at checkout.
If an acidic beverage is spilled onto the coaster, just rinse with water to protect the image. If grease or oil comes into contact with the coaster, wash the surface with mild soap and warm water and then rinse. Do not put in the dishwasher. It is advised to seal the coaster (provided by us free of charge if you specify the need) if it will be coming into regular contact with highly acidic or oily substances (wine or casserole dishes). If you are using the stone as a candle holder, some candles are also high in oil content and it is recommended that a glass barrier (small clear dish) be placed between the candle and the stone to protect the images. Lastly, stone can break if mishandled or dropped. We do our absolute best to ship as safely as possible.
Photo images are a representation of the item(s) you will be receiving. Because the stone used is a tumbled marble product, shape or color may differ slightly, but will stay true to the beautiful design that you see. You will not be disappointed!

ALUMINIUM: A soft, versitile and lightweight metal that is a great price alternative to Sterling Silver. Aside from being low in cost, aluminum does not tarnish - If the metal becomes dull or dirty it can be easily wiped away with a lint free cloth / silver cloth. This soft metal, however, is not as strong as Sterling Silver and continued bending and twisting will weaken the metal and inevitably break. Aluminium is perfect for bangles and bracelets because it's rare that it causes a reaction making it ideal for wearers with more sensitive skin.
COPPER: A hard metal that has a lovely earthy red colour. Known for it’s possible medicinal benefits. Copper can cause slight green discoloration of the skin, this is due to the metal reacting to the natural acids in your skin & the oxygen in the air. As Copper does oxidize quickly, it often has a darker appearance, which can be removed easily with a Copper cloth / Sunshine Cloth / Pro Polish Pad to reveal its beautiful red finish.
To care for your copper, a good tip is to use a very small mixture of water, vinegar and a tiny bit of salt to clean. Make sure you polish it regularly using a polishing cloth to remove any residue.
SILVER PLATED: Silver Plate is described as "covering something with a thin layer of silver" all of our silver plated items have a base metal of either either brass or steel which are then copper coated & then silver plated, these contain less then 5% nickle which is compliant with EU legislation.
To care for your silver plated cutlery, it's always best to hand wash and not use a dishwasher. Don’t let it come into contact with stainless steel as this can cause corrosion as the metals react. Ensure you dry each piece by hand and use a flannel cloth and specialised silver polish (or a silver polishing cloth) to maintain the lustrous 
shine.
STAINLESS STEEL: A super strong and hugely durable metal. Stainless steel is hypoallergenic making it ideal for people who tend to have a reaction to other metals.
Stainless steel will not rust, tarnish or stain and retains its high shine with little effort on your behalf.
To care for your stainless steel, all you need is warm water, a cloth and dish washing soap. After cleaning, simply polish it lightly with a dry cloth to remove any water spots.
WILL MY PIECE RESIST TARNISHING?
All metals may mar or scratch with wear/friction & will age over time based on frequency of use. They may also tarnish or damage depending on the PH of the body & the circumstances of wear; in the shower, pool, prolonged sun exposure, during sleep etc.
I'VE ACCIDENTALLY SNAGGED MY CHAIN AND IT HAS BROKEN, WHAT CAN I DO?
Unfortunately small accidents happens, and even though our delicate pieces are designed to be worn everyday, they are not indestructible. If you'd like, you can send your piece in for repair and we will re-fit new jump rings and chain, if required, and send it straight back out to you. Please do contact me before sending out your piece, I can then help with instructions & the best way to send your piece to us along with a custom quote & timescale.
- Polish your jewelry after wearing to remove oils, fingerprints & dust.
- Keep your jewelry as dry as possible. Do not store it in a humid environment.
- To keep your jewelry nice and shiny, store it in a re-sealable plastic bag with anti-tarnish paper. Make sure your jewelry is clean and moisture free before storing.
- Do not wear in the shower/ swimming pool /hot tub. Chlorinated water can react with the metals causing color changes and even structural damage.
- Remove jewelry before any vigorous activity, before sleeping & when performing manual tasks (kitchen work, gardening, cleaning the house) to prevent physical damage or exposure to chemicals or cleaning fluids.
- Put jewelry on after applying makeup – Cosmetics, hairspray, perfumes and lotion can contain chemicals that can often damage jewelry.
- These metals will naturally oxidize/tarnish over time, due to exposure to air and oils from our skin.
- If you want to restore the shine, remove LIGHT tarnish stains and build-up from your jewelry piece, use JUST a polishing pad (foam square with micro-abrasives already built in). Silver polishing cloth will not work on copper or brass.
HOW TO USE YOUR POLISHING PAD: Gently rub a pad across a piece of jewelry that is completely dry and store your piece in an air-tight plastic bag. When cleaning chains, hold by the clasp and do not tug at the chain or you risk breaking the clasp.
-The "black" in your hand stamped items is patina, it may wear off over time and exposure to certain elements. However, you can take care of your items to prolong the life of the patina.
- To clean your handstamped jewelry, simply polish with a jewelry cleaning cloth.
- HAND STAMPED jewelry should NOT be cleaned with any jewelry cleaning solution, as the solution can rub off the oxidation (patina) that's in the letter indentions.
- Avoid submerging your jewelry in water, cleaning supplies or chlorine pools.
- Avoid exposing your jewelry to household chemicals when cleaning with bleach or ammonia, or when swimming in chlorinated water, as these chemicals can damage silver. Perfumes, hair sprays, and profuse sweating can also cause a quicker formation of tarnish.
- REMOVE AT NIGHT. Do not sleep with plated jewelry, night sweat and the extra rubbing against the skin will cause the plating to wear off faster.
- STORE LIKE ITEMS TOGETHER. Do not put away gold plating and silver plating together. The different metals will cause each other to tarnish, fade and/or turn colors. Store in a dry, dark area.
- DO NOT CLEAN WITH CHEMICALS. Plating is much more delicate than pure metals, chemicals will fade the plating.
Clean often to keep shine and remove sweat & dirt that will cause items to fade. Use a damp cloth and wipe down gently, use a clean towel to dry. When cleaning chains hold by the clasp and do not tug at the chain or you risk breaking the clasp.

For a snug fit, add 1/2” to the size; for a looser fit, add 1” to the size.
This is not a guarantee for a perfect fit, but it is what most people recommend.

By purchasing my work containing small and possibly detachable elements you recognize the potential risks and are fully responsible for the its prevention.<|endoftext|>On January 1, rules will take effect that will impact Etsy shops selling digital items to buyers in the EU.
Starting January 1, 2015, there will be significant changes to European Commission rules related to Value Added Tax (VAT) on sales of digital goods and services to consumers in Europe. The new rules state that all businesses selling digital goods and delivering them electronically to customers in European Union member countries will be required to pay VAT based on the VAT rates of the country where the customer is located, not on the rates of the country where the business is located. If your shop is based outside of the EU, it is unclear how the VAT rules will be enforced.
Some Etsy shop owners have asked if Etsy will be handling VAT payments on digital goods under the new rules. Historically, Etsy has acted as a venue on which individual entrepreneurs run their businesses, with Etsy sellers responsible for paying appropriate sales taxes for those businesses. We are treating VAT the same way, with sellers expected to collect and pay VAT.
We understand that the new regulations will be an added burden for shops that sell digital items and deliver them electronically to EU customers and we’re working on a tool that will make the process easier for you. We will be releasing more details in early 2015. The EU is also attempting to make the VAT payment process easier by allowing businesses based in member countries to opt for simplified VAT registration and return filing, known as mini one-stop shop, or MOSS. Get more information about mini one-stop shops on the European Commission website.
For more information about the new VAT rules, read this FAQ. Learn more about how VAT works on Etsy in this Help Article.
Visit the European Union Commission website for more information. If you are an Etsy seller based in the EU, look for information on requirements specific to your country.
We encourage you to consult with a tax professional for specific advice about your business.
1) Providing information on buyer countries: Beginning in January, you’ll be able to verify the country of your buyers.
2) Control over where you sell items: We’ve heard from you that you’d like to be able to control the countries in which you sell digital items. We are looking into the feasibility of this and will update you in early 2015.
Some of you have also asked if the new VAT rules apply to digital items that are delivered to customers by email. At least in the UK, the government has taken the position that PDFs manually emailed by sellers are not covered by the new rules. We will continue to provide updates as soon as we have new information.

DESIGN STUDIO + STORE NOW OPEN!
My design process begins with inspiration- from a song, a newly discovered locale, another artist, a fabric, a contour of the body, or a feeling that something is missing from my own wardrobe. I create my patterns mainly through draping, and sew many muslins, up to 10 or 12, to perfect the fit.
Everything is created by me in-house from start to finish, with the exception of a few pieces that require specialty machinery during finishing. I get outside help with buttonholes, pressing, specialty seaming & leather application from skilled local artists who have the equipment and expertise.
My philosophy is that good design is created mindfully within the context of the bigger picture: how our actions as women and as consumers impact our lives, the lives of others and the planet. My vision is to support the transitions taking place in women’s lives as they embrace change, and their shift toward making more sustainable choices.
In 2012, I was named as one of Canada’s top 15 Eco Designers in ECOHOLIC BODY, the new book by author and blogger Adria Vasil. I also became a member of Fashion Takes Action, a not-for-profit organization which connects with both consumers and industry professionals to educate, inform and assist them in making sustainable choices.
Seeing a growing gap in ladies fashion, and feeling the need to reflect my re-direction in aesthetics and philosophy, I retired my first label Device and launched Vespertine in the fall of 2013. Vespertine is unique, providing women in their prime with figure-flattering designs in structured fabrics that give them a polished, pulled-together look- sustainably. The contemporary ladies wear line is produced in Toronto, Canada and is available in sizes 2-16 or XS-XXXL.
Vespertine's signature style is inspired by the many incarnations of the modern woman: conscious, effortless, and always, beautiful.

Vespertine sizing is based on the following body measurements: Bust (the circumference around the widest area of the bust), Waist (circumference of the smallest part of your waist, where the measuring tape will naturally settle), and Hips (circumference of the widest part of your hips and rear). I work in inches.
2/XS: Bust 33" Waist 26" Hips 36"
4/S: Bust 35" Waist 28" Hips 38"
6/M: Bust 37" Waist 30" Hips 40"
8/L: Bust 39" Waist 32" Hips 42"
10/XL: Bust 41" Waist 34" Hips 44"
12/XXL: Bust 43" Waist 36" Hips 46"
14/XXL: Bust 45-47" Waist 34-36" Hips 44-46"
16/XXXL:Bust 47" Waist 36" Hips 46"
To take your measurements accurately, wear snug clothing and stand in front of a mirror. The tape should stay parallel to the floor, and float over the body without pulling- too much tension will squeeze the body and cause errors.
No measuring tape? Here's a great tip: use a length of string, ribbon or cord instead. Mark off your circumference where the ends meet, then remove the string and measure between markings with a ruler.
If you don't see your size listed on the chart, or if you are unsure which size is best for you, please convo me and I'll be happy to advise. Depending on the item, I may be able to do a custom size- be sure to include your measurements, and any any special considerations (eg. height).
WHAT EXACTLY IS SUSTAINABILITY, AND HOW DOES IT RELATE TO FASHION?
Sustainability is the capacity to endure. For us humans, it is the potential for long-term maintenance of well being, achieved by creating systems which can be supported indefinitely in terms of environmental and social responsibility. Sustainable fashion describes designs that are created and produced with consideration 
to the environmental and social impact they will have throughout their creation and life span. Those considerations include waste reduction, recycling, textile sourcing, labour practices and quality control.
If you like an item but wish it came in another colour, convo me and I may be able to accommodate you with a custom order. Please be aware that individual computer screens may display colours slightly differently.
I'm always interested in hearing your requests for custom orders! Whether it is a variation of an existing item in the shop, a custom size or a completely custom design, please convo me to discuss.
ARE THESE GARMENTS MACHINE WASHABLE?
All items come labelled with washing and care instructions. Most non-wool pieces are either machine or hand washable and should be hung or laid flat to dry. Dryers will shorten the life of any garment. I highly recommend a phosphate-free laundry soap. Eco-friendly laundering is a powerful (and easy) way you can "green" your wardrobe. See below for more information.

Since the illustrations are hand drawn, it is an edition variee. While they are extremely similar, the illustrations make it impossible for each book to be exactly the same. I think it adds charm. This listing is for one book from my 6 book edition.
The letterpress type in this book was created on a Vandercook Print Press at Texas Woman's University. I used some fabulous big metal type to create impressions on watercolor paper with hand torn edges. The illustrations are inked and then painted on top with watercolors.
There are seven pairings in the book. The book is 9 1/2" H x 6" W. The book has 20 pages and 14 hand drawn illustrations. Each pair is a wine and cheese that I love best together. I had to do some serious research. In this case, a lot of wine and cheese had to be consumed. It's a hard job, but someone has to do it.
Although lighthearted in many ways, the book also poses my thoughts about pairings and how I feel our culture presents that we are better or more whole if we are coupled up with that special someone. Each pairing has their own phrase associated with this idea, such as "two peas in a pod" or "coupling". You see the wine and cheese together, overlaid through a window that showcases the matched set and both of their best qualities. When you turn the page, the cheese stands alone and the wine is left incomplete, with a hole in the bottle.
This book was made with much care and love and each element was carefully selected by the artist, from the lovely papers to the hand drawn and watercolored images. It is sure to make you thirsty and hungry.

Garment/Item is in perfect original or restored condition. It is not damaged or faded in any way. All original details and decorations are intact and no alterations or changes to the original item have been made. It’s possible that this item was never worn.
Garment/Item is intact but the lining, decorations or item details show some signs of wear. There are no tears, fading, holes, wear spots, fraying or splitting. Very, very faint yellowing or fading are reasons an item may labeled as very good.
Garment/Item is intact and ready to wear (except for a missing button, maybe).. The outside of the item shows no significant tears, fading, holes, wear spots, fraying or splitting. The item shows expected signs of wear for its age, may have a button missing (will be noted), seams that are coming loose but not yet holes, or crinkling of belts. Besides light fading or wrinkling on belts, flaws on good items are easily fixed The item still 
has a long life ahead of it..
Garment/Item is wearable or usable but may have stains, minor holes and fading, and missing buttons and decorations. Faded, missing more than one button, or hole at seam or hem. If it’s more than just fading, the repair is usually an easy one that could be hand-stitched or repaired by a tailor. Visible fading or significant pilling could get an item into this category. Flaws that may be covered by hair, a brooch, a belt, etc. may fall into this category if the rest of the garment is in good condition.
These items are offered at a highly discounted rate and represent great value for the person who’s willing to put in some effort or really use their creative juices. Rarely do we sell items in this condition, and if we do it’s because the item is unique or awesome enough that it deserves a second chance. There’s either a decent sized hole or a rip that’s located somewhere besides a hem or seam. These items are great for somebody who’s up to a challenge (patching, stitching, covering a flaw with applique, etc). The garment cannot be worn as is. Can I change the color(s) of the decal?
Yes, all of our decals can be ordered in your choice of over 60 colors. Please see the color chart that is in the picture viewer on every listing.
Can I change the name on the decal?
Of course, we have a large selection of personalized wall decals. We can change the name on any of them.
Will your decals stick to my painted walls?
We cannot guarantee our decals will stick to your specific walls/paint. Therefore we strongly recommend you order a paint test decal to test compatibility of our product. Our vinyl decals can be applied to most smooth to lightly textured surfaces. Freshly painted surfaces must dry for at least two weeks before application of decal. The out-gassing of the paint on the first two weeks can cause a decal to fail.
Important note: Vinyl wall decals have been found to have lower adhesion levels with some types of No VOC paints as well as paints containing stain blocker additives or "easy clean" paints. If you have used one of these paints I strongly recommend you order a paint test decal to test compatibility of our product.

Are your vinyl decals removable, can they damage my walls?
Our decals remove with ease and will not damage your paint, walls, ceilings or floors.

Yes, if you see another font you like better on a different listing let us know and we can change it. Or you can simply convo us for a selection of fonts.<|endoftext|>Materials: Rich + Vibrant, archival quality,

Originating from early 17th century pirate-lore, seashells made into pipes and coated with plant resins have been found in numerous shipwrecks. The plunder of British East India Company vessels brought to many pirates delight, in the finding of exquisite herbs cultivated in India being exported to South Africa and Jamaica. Not all treasure is silver and gold!
ShellPipe™ is your source for nature's coolest pipes!
They're stronger than borosilicate, and won't shatter like glass if dropped!
More is better, we include free pipes in every order!
Just as with all smoking devices, ShellPipes require cleaning to ensure smooth tokes. Screens will get oil buildup faster than your pipe, and are easier to clean in order for your pipe to smoke well. Pull out the screen and holding it with a metal tool, light the screen on fire to burn any buildup off. Once cool, flex the screen and rub clean then insert back in your pipe.
Complete cleaning is very basic. Soak your ShellPipe in alcohol for several hours, or boil in water for 15 to 20 minutes to clean out just about all resin buildup. Smaller pipes such as the Archimedes tend to chip if you burn the pipe getting the flame too close. Watch out for this, but in case it does happen simply break off the remaining chips to even the bowl and push the screen deeper. If you want a smooth feel to the bowl again, lightly rubbing with sandpaper or a nail file will clean up your ShellPipe nicely!

Hello, I'm glad that you stopped by my Etsy shop today! Let me introduce myself -- I'm Suzanne Shelton. If you can't already tell it, I'm a southern girl, born and raised in Mississippi. After getting my Computer Engineering degree from Mississippi State, I moved to the North Alabama area because this was the closest job I could find to home. That was over 20 years ago! I now call Alabama home.
Now, let me tell you a little about how and why I started Olivia Anne Designs in the summer of 2006. A group of ladies were meeting to help a friend plan a “Christmas in July” emphasis for her quilt shop. Someone said “We need a pattern for a Christmas stocking!” and I just so happened to have an original design that I had been making for family and friends for several years. This became my first pattern! Once my “Jungle Jubilee” pattern came along, I had several requests for me to teach classes on how to applique these designs onto children’s clothing. To make the classes flow smoother and to avoid sending the students home with unfinished projects, I had the designs cut out and put together for the them so all they had to do was iron them down and stitch around the shapes. This led to the creation of what I call my “Ready Set Appliques” – in simpler terms, these are “iron-on appliques”. These turned out to be extremely popular and I started drawing animals and other things as stand-alone designs.
For the business’ first six years, I concentrated on whimsical 
appliques for children’s clothing and baby quilts. As more and more of my wholesale customers unfortunately had to shut down their fabric businesses, I realized that I had to make some changes too if I wanted the business to continue. However, not only was the sewing industry going through a makeover, I found that my interests were evolving also. At this same time, we were remodeling our house to provide me with a much dreamed about studio space. With this addition, I found that I had so much more freedom to look at other possibilities for the business. My appliques and applique patterns are still around, but I’m starting to use them on other things besides fabric. For example, I now have notecards, hand-colored, framed prints, embellished frames, and door or wall art. I still sew children’s clothes, but these will be more “one of a kind” items.
Through all of the changes that both my business and I have undergone over the past several years, I still believe in my two main goals: 1) I want to make you smile every time you see one of my creations and 2) I want to publicly give God the credit for any success. In high school, I learned the scripture verse Jeremiah 29:11, “For I know the plans that I have for you, says the Lord. They are plans for good and not for evil, to give you a future and a hope.” I really believe this verse! I am learning to trust Him more each day. When I look back on my past, it is amazing to see how His Plan is unfolding in my life.
Thanks for stopping by. I hope you will take a look around. If you like what you see, please, tell your friends about us!

Glad you asked! A Printable is an electronic file in PDF format that allows you to print our designs at your convenience. Print when you want and how many you want. Again and again.
What do you mean by "editable" or "semi-customizable"?
This is where you get to unleash your creativity. You can enter and format your own text right in the Printable. That means you can change the font, font size, font color, and font alignment to create a wide variety of looks all from the same Printable. Please keep in mind you can't change the color(s), size or position of the design graphics in the file.
Can I add graphics or jpegs to the Printables?
The Printables can accommodate text (fonts) only not jpegs or TIFFs etc. You can use fonts that contain images (like dingbats) to insert an image.
How do I receive my Printable?
Your Printable file(s) will be emailed to the email associated with your ETSY account (unless you let me know differently) within 24 hours. If you have not received your file within 24 hours, first please check your Junk or Spam folder, then contact me at hello [!at] whiskergraphics.com.
Do I have to be a computer genius to use the Printables?
Genius? No. But it's helpful if you have a little computer experience under your belt. You'll need to be familiar with opening a file, selecting fonts and font styles and printing.
You can use any font you have installed on your computer including fonts that contain images or icons (like flowers or animals). You can also use multiple fonts in the same text box.
The files work only in Adobe Reader 8 or newer. You can download this program for FREE at www.adobe.com. The files will not open in Illustrator or Photoshop.
How do I get the Properties Toolbar to show in Adobe Reader so I can format my text?
Due to the nature of the files, you will not be able to save the Printable with your entered information. For that reason, we suggest you print out some extras before closing the file. You can also create and format your text in MS Word (save the file for future use) and copy/paste into the Printable.
Do I have to format my text in every text box again and again?
In the Amazing 3" Squares all text boxes (6) are independent of each other. If you want the same info in all the boxes, format your text in one text box and copy/paste into the remaining text boxes.
In the Amazing 2" Squares, text boxes are set up to auto-fill by row. Format your text in one box, click outside the box and the remaining squares in that row will fill in with the same formatted information. Need all 20 squares with the same info? No problem. Just format your text in one box then copyp/paste it into the first box in each row.
In our Printable Stationery sets, the whole page 
of return address labels fills in automatically after you enter your text in one label and then click in another label.
What's so amazing about your 2" and 3" squares?
Well, we think it's pretty amazing that you can create so many different things from one Printable.
All the Printables are created to print on 8.5 x 11" sheets unless otherwise noted. We like to use 80lb or heavier white card stock for cards, tags, recipe cards and mini file folders, but really you can print on any paper you like. Keep in mind that if you print on colored paper it will alter the appearance of the colors in the Printable.
If you want to make labels from the Printables, you'll need 8.5 x 11" full sheet labels. Basically one, big 8.5 x 11" label. They can easily be found at office supply stores or on the web (search "full sheet labels").
Will the Printables work on pre-cut labels?
We hate to disappoint, but no. Each printer feeds paper/label sheets differently which can cause a lot of frustration when trying to line up images on pre-cut labels. To ensure the best results, we've created our Printables to print on full sheet labels only. There are clearly marked trim lines to show you where to cut.
Will the Printable work on a Mac?
The Printables should work just fine on a Mac. The default PDF viewer on a Mac is called Preview. So if you're working on a Mac, make sure you open the Printable in Adobe Reader 8 or newer.
Can I share with my friends and family?
When you purchase a Printable from us, you are buying a 1-person personal (non-commercial) license to use the Printable. So, feel free to create as many items as you like (stationery, recipe cards and gift tags make great gifts!) and print as many times as you like to share what you/ve made with your family and friends, but the file is only for the purchaser.
Is there a limit to how many times I can print a Printable?
The skys the limit! Make cards for friends and family, bookplates for teachers or recipe cards for everyone at the potluck. The file is yours to print forever.
Can I add pages to the Recipe Card Printables file?
The Printables are designed to produce physical paper goods, not as an electronic management system. Therefore, you will not be able to add pages to any of the Printable files.
Hey, I have a question that isn't answered here!
Chances are if you have a question we haven't answered, someone else will have the same question. Drop us a note at hello [!at] whiskergraphics.com.<|endoftext|>Your wedding should be as unique as you are, so this multi-functional custom-made signpost should fit right into your special day. NamiZuni Jewelry: wearable art to express your creative spirit.
Nancie Zimmerman has been creating art since she was a tiny girl in Bucks County, Pennsylvania. Her grandmas, Nama and Judy, taught her how to crochet, knit, sew, and create cards from buttons, fabric scraps, and paint. She experimented with every craft she could get her hands on...crewel, embroidery, paint by numbers, sand art, decoupage, macrame, and quilting.
Now living in the San Francisco Bay Area, Nancie happened upon jewelry making when a group of crafting friends got together to make wine charms. Nancie's friends always teased her that anytime they crafted together, she would obsessively be experimenting with new ideas long after everyone else had tired of the project. So it was with the wine charms. Once Nancie realized that the charms could easily be made into earrings, her passion for jewelry making began.
When Nancie began tossing around ideas for the name of her business, she happened upon NamiZuni when a magazine subscription accidentally entered her name as "Nami Zuni" instead of "Nancie Zimmerman" (not even close, right?). Soon Nami Zuni began receiving brochures for exotic trips and catalogs for expensive products, leading Nancie to quip that Nami Zuni was living Nancie's dream life.
NamiZuni came to represent Nancie's inner goddess, helping her fashion wearable art that allows you express your own stylish, creative spirit. NamiZuni Jewelry makes you feel good every time you wear her pieces...allowing your own inner goddess to shine through.
Be sure to look for the soon-to-be-available “Beads for Hope” section, which features beads bought from impoverished female artisans from around the world. This coat pattern from 1934 has princess seams, raglan sleeves, and a lovely large collar. It fastens with one button at the waist. This coat can be made in one fabric or made in two with a contrast fabric or fur collar. We suggest using faux fur.
This pattern’s original instructions are very minimal, which is true to the period. These instructions tell how to put the basic coat together. We have added basic tips and watchpoints for working with this pattern. If you wish to do more detailed tailoring, we suggest using a tailoring book in addition to these instructions.
NOT a multi-size pattern. We ran into issues with multi sizing, but instead of not offering the pattern at all, we decided to offer it in the original size so current sewing enthusiasts can enjoy it.
Finished length from back of neck about 50 1/2”.
Width at lower edge about 1 5/8 yards.
Collar, 50 Inch Fur Cloth- 5/8 yards.
This pattern is tiled into letter sized paper. You will print these documents on your home printer, cut, and tape them together, to form a larger pattern layout. Then you cut and use your pattern just as you would a normal home sewing pattern.
64 total sheets of 8.5" x 11" sized paper or A4 sized paper are needed. This pattern file is formatted to fit on both sizes of paper, and there will be varying thicknesses of white border, which will be cut off, according to pattern instructions.

As this story begins, my husband took a job in Columbia, Maryland and I was not a happy camper, to say the least. Of all the little cities I visited, I found this quaint little Counted Cross Stitch Shop in Ellicott City and when I stepped inside, I discovered I was at home. The owner was a charming lady from the United Kingdom and she taught me how to do counted cross stitch without a hoop. Because of this, I was able to cross stitch quicker and of course I was buying more patterns. So to make a long story short, I was paying all kinds of money to have my cross stitch pieces framed.
When my husband's company went out of business, we returned home and I decided to go to school to learn how to be a picture framer. Where can I buy elastic?
Check out eBay for 5/16" or 1/4" knitted elastic. I always used a seller by the name of ny-sale.
For some reason, the sewing pattern seems to have printed too large or too small, what do I do?
In Adobe Acrobat Reader, make sure your settings are set to "Actual Size" before hitting the print button, otherwise the printer will often shrink to fit or stretch to fit it to the printer paper, thus distorting the sewing pattern.
What type of fabric do you use for posing suits and bikinis?
For the top fabric, always use a 4-way stretch fabric, and for the liner fabric, I always loved using either swim 4-way stretch liner, or 4-way stretch cotton lycra.
What's the best glue for gluing on rhinestones?
E-6000 is my favorite, but be careful, it does have fumes that need ventilated. Read all safety information before use.
What types of rhinestones do you recommend?
I always use the glass-type rhinestones, such as Swarovski, Preciosa, or Allora. Avoid using acrylic, and stick to flat back rhinestones. I do not like using hotfix, only due to the fact that they take longer to apply.
My most used sizes for rhinestones are 16ss, 20ss, and 30ss on suits.
Where do you buy bra pads?
Unfortunately, this is my MOST frequently asked question, as well as most difficult one to answer. I used to have a local supplier, but they went out of business. It is very difficult to find sellers, but my recommendation is to search here on Etsy because we have a great resource of sellers.
Due to this being so difficult, I created a sewing pattern, that's now in my store, that specifically addresses the issue by teaching you how to create your own foam cup for a molded cup top. It is the Classic Style Top, go check it out!
I am having trouble with a certain step in the sewing process, help!
Please check out my sewing videos at youtube.com/jodilane because I have several helpful sewing videos that address some of the more complicated steps! I hope this helps!
Husqvarna Emerald 183. I purchased it in 2011, and it's still going strong! Which ever machine you choose, I highly recommend one with a drop-in bobbin. They are the absolute BEST.
What stitches does my machine need to have to be able use your patterns?
All your machine needs is the ability to do a straight stitch and a zig zag stitch. My sewing patterns are designed so that anyone can use them with the simplest of tools!<|endoftext|>Show your viewers the stars with these out of this world babies! The Milky Way has never looked so good!

Bringing My Dream to Reality!
There is a reason behind why I make these bracelets and I call them "A Grateful Heart". In 2011 I made my first bracelet because of a dream I had. I had never tried beading before and knew nothing about beading. In the dream there was this wonderful white flowing divine spirit angel showing me how to make this bracelet. A lot of times I have dreams or visions that be telling me how to do stuff. So, no I'm not batty or crazy so don't laugh. I'm just a little tad different, that's all. You know some people are like that. In the dream I was given the beads, charms, and cord string etc., everything I needed to make the bracelet. I needed crystal clear beads that sparkle with a rainbow color, a heart and cross charms that sparkle as well. The angel spirit told me that the heart charm is used to represent having a grateful heart in life. The cross charm is used for God's love and blessings in my life. I wanted to spice up the bracelets I'm now making to sell with crystals with some color in it, so I did. After finishing the bracelet in my dream it was very beautiful and sparkles so bright. The angel spirit told me that I am to wear this bracelet all the time for it is to serve as a reminder of me having a grateful heart in life. That anytime my eyes catch a glimpse of my sparkly beautiful bracelet I was to at that moment in time write down something I was grateful for. When I woke up I felt so happy and good inside and anxious to make this bracelet. I went to Michael's craft store to find the items I needed to make my bracelet. My bracelet came out pretty and people noticed it and complimented how pretty it was. I wore it all the time but removed it when showering, washing dishes etc. I really took good care of it and handle it delicately for not to break it.
There was a lesson in this dream for me. I never really thought about being grateful in life until I had that dream. I thought giving thanks was just for Thanksgiving Day. This dream opened my eyes to let me know we can give thanks every day in life, not just for the holidays. I learned also, when we are thankful and appreciative of our blessings we already have in life... that can bring more blessings into your life. We all have something to be thankful for every day. I love life and very grateful for each day I wake up and I give thanks for that and there are a lot more things I'm grateful for. I could ramble off a long list but I will stop right here. I'm sure you can understand what I mean. Each day I find myself writing down something I am thankful for. From that day forth of that dream I understood it and obeyed what I was supposed to do.
I make these bracelets because of this dream. I thought this will be a wonderful way to share my inspirational message. Wear this bracelet to serve as a reminder to have a grateful heart for the blessings in your life. This will make a lovely gift for yourself, family and friends!

Ashford Corriedale sliver is a 100% New Zealand product and by far a favorite wool roving for both traditional wet felting and dry needle felting. The wool is from pasture-fed sheep from farmers – some of whom have farmed the land for generations. They take great pride in the quality of their wool and the high standard of animal husbandry. The sheep are well cared for and are not mulesed.
After the sheep are shorn, on the farm, the wool is carefully skirted and checked. Only wool that is sound, clean with good fiber length, bulk and color is selected. It is sent to a boutique New Zealand mill to be hand dyed, carded and combed.
It is washed using an environmentally-friendly, biodegradable detergent. The wool is then dried and dyed. The dyes comply with the strict EU regulations and the roving can be certified under the "Oeko-Tex Standard 100". This standard is the most widely known standard for certification

How should I use the catnip?
For best results, pinch some catnip between your fingers and crush the leaves to help release the potent oils. Sprinkle the catnip and silver vine blend where your cat likes to play! If you cat doesn't react to catnip and silver vine, try one of our other catnip blends!

Tea can stay safe to drink for quite a long time! In fact, other than nutrients decaying over time, so long as it still smells and tastes good, it's perfectly fine to drink! However, if you do want to make sure that you're getting all those awesome nutrients, it's agreed upon that about a year will be what to aim for.
Of course, to lengthen that time, you can keep your tea in the freezer!
Thankfully, all my tea is made fresh, and packaged in resealable bags! I also like to keep my ingredients as fresh as possible, so I make orders for the ingredients for as much as I would need to make tea in a month, so your bags of tea will be pretty darn fresh when you get them!

When the light hits this designer pen it shimmers with a depth that produces a kaleidoscope effect. This high quality pen is one of the nicer handmade ink pens you will find. Pretty pens such as this are wonderful gifts for any occasion. Treat yourself or someone you know to this beautiful pen today!
The cool pen that is pictured is the pen that the buyer will receive.
Pen size: 5.75" long, .5" at it's widest point.
First the pen blank was made by wrapping strips of holographic tape onto a brass tube. The tube was then cast in clear resin. The tape catches the light and sparkles, giving the pen a three dimensional appearance. Both ends of the cast tube were sanded flush to the brass tube. Then I mounted the pen blank onto a wood lathe. Using hand tools, I turned the blank down to it's final shape making certain that the ends of the blank were just the right size to match up to the components of the pen. I then sanded and polished the blank to an crystal clear finish. I then attached the components to the pen blank with a special press and a small drop of adhesive.

Tell Me About Your Mugs.
Our mugs are designed by Sarah, then individually hand pressed in our home studio using professional grade sublimation equipment for a dishwasher and microwave safe finish.
The design is printed on both sides of the mug, so they are perfect whether you are right handed or left handed. (The only exception is mugs with long calligraphy swashes that wrap around the side. Printing on both sides would cause these swashes to overlap).
We offer both 11oz and 15oz sizes as well as two color options (an all-white mug and a white mug with black handle & trim). Each mug is carefully shipped, double boxed with a sturdy white gift box and insured against damage.
Tell Me About Your Silverware.
We source the highest quality antique and vintage silverware, using only table-ready pieces with no pitting or plate loss. We never use “craft-grade” or “shabby” flatware. Our silverware is authentic vintage silver-plate, not reproductions.
We hammer in every letter one at a time by hand, never with machine presses or engraving equipment. The resulting impressions are a permanent feature of the silverware, so our nearly million hammer blows of experience come in handy to be sure every letter, punctuation, and heart ends up exactly where we want it!
Hand washing is recommended to protect the silver plating. Silver naturally tarnishes when exposed to oxygen, but you can easily remove tarnish and restore shine by using silver polish.
Tell Me About Your Wood Products.
We source our cutting boards here in the Virginia countryside, working with a local company with nearly a century of experience in wood making. We choose beautiful maple and cherry hardwoods, then precision engrave our custom designs onto them in our Virginia studio. We do not use chemicals, stains, or varnish on our cutting boards.
Since we make each one ourselves, we can offer a limitless number of personalization options and love collaborating with our customers to create a special piece just for you.
Our cutting boards are hand-wash only. Please do not submerge or place in dishwasher.
What Silver Pattern Will I Receive?
We have many individually photographed pieces that show you the exact piece you will receive. Our made-to-order listings will vary depending on what patterns are in the studio when you order.
We are very careful to stock only table-ready silverware with no plate loss or pitting, never using “shabby” or “craft grade” silverware. We also curate a wide assortment of styles, 
so if you have a personal preference (floral, simple, masculine, etc.), please let us know in a note at checkout and we will choose the perfect piece.
While we are happy to send you photographs of silver styles to choose from, this does delay the production process by a few days and we will need to update your ship-by date to reflect this.
My Mug Arrived Broken, What Now?
In the rare instance that a mug arrives cracked or broken, we will replace it for you at no charge and handle the insurance claim with the postal service.
USPS requires us to send a photograph of the broken mug and the original packaging. If you could please send that to us at your convenience, we will then get right to work shipping you a replacement mug.
I Don't Want To Pay Customs Fees. Can You Mark the Package as "Gift"?
I'm sorry but we are unable to honor requests to falsify customs documents.

Honoloulou's...it all started with a shark!
Honoloulou's was born from my passion for creativity, a love of the ocean, and desire to make beautiful shark jewellery with a bit of a difference. Each of the items available is designed and handmade by me, and there's a whole lot of love that goes into creating each one!
Unfortunately many shark populations have been decimated due to years of being hunted for their teeth, fins, meat, oil, as trophies for sports fisherman, or caught in fishing lines and nets, and so £1 or more from each necklace sold will be donated to a marine conservation charity working to protect sharks and their ocean habitat.
Donations so far have gone to The Shark Trust, or which Honolouou's is an official commercial supporter, and Shark4Kids. You can find out more about them and the fabulous work they do by visiting their websites.
Buying a Honoloulou's necklace will not only make you look good, but feel good too.
Follow me on Facebook if you'd like to hear first about new designs, promotions and lots and lots of news about sharks and ocean conservation. Be great to see you there!
You can also follow me on Instagram for lot and lots of sharks photos, and the odd one of my cat in all manner of strange poses!
If you'd like to read a little bit more about me, Honoloulou's, and my love of sharks, you can read the Sharks4Kids blog for which I was the February featured artist this year.
I'm Louise. I live in Bristol in the UK, and I set up Honoloulou's in August of 2014. All of the items in my shop are handmade by me, and express my love of the sharks and the ocean.

So Many Flowers! was conceived of around 15 years ago. I wanted something to do that was creative and completely different from my day job. I've loved flowers and anything to do with flowers, forever. I've grown them, sold them, admired them, arranged them and studied them. Pressing them was new to me, however. I started small, collecting and pressing and making pictures and labeling the flowers. These proved to be rather popular and my enthusiasm for starting a business grew from there. Little by little I've increased my efforts, moved past the "hobby" definition and now call myself a business, creating pressed flower art. Previously the primary method of selling my work has been through craft shows and galleries. Now I am offering my work to the world, through Etsy!
Art for me is a constructive process based on my imagination and a thorough understanding of materials. When I prepare to design a picture, I have a particular frame in mind so the frame and picture complete an integrated piece of art. I begin with the bones of the picture, possibly trees, background mountains or other large objects, then complete the piece by filling in with the plants and flowers that would grow in that location. In my art, flowers and other botanicals serve as my paint, and my goal is to make the picture resemble and celebrate nature as we observe it.
My lifelong love of plants and flowers inspires me, daily, to make art that reflects the beauty and serenity of a walk in the woods.
Nature calls to me. It's my motivation for making art that reflects the natural world. The colors of wildflowers, textures of botanical materials, mountain vistas and landscapes all contribute to my inspiration. This variety makes each work unique.

This shop is a place where I share a collection of cozy gifts created for you. From wedding décor jar covers to crochet blankets and accessories, like beanies and scarves. Everything is thoughtfully handmade by yours truly.
I began crocheting around the age of eleven. I adored the cozy blankets that my grandma had made and asked my mother to teach me. Looking back, I can remember sitting on the hearth together as she taught me how to magically transform a skein of yarn into beautiful stitches and eventually a scarf.
There is a scene in my favorite movie, Breakfast At Tiffanys, where Holly claims her knitting pattern for a sweater morphed into a ranch house after a pattern mix up. Well, that was quite similar to the way I had trouble following patterns. They just weren't my thing. Therefore I went my own way and after several lopsided scarves and awkward beanies, I honed my craft and created my own designs and patterns. Even now, although I learned how to follow a pattern without crocheting a ranch house, I love dreaming up my own ideas. Mixing different stitches and watching a skein of yarn magically transform into something I've imagined is so rewarding.
You may have guessed from the shop name, I am Rachel Allison. When I originally established my shop on Etsy in 2012, I chose to name it Anchor In Time. Geared more towards my love of the ocean and everything nautical, it fit. Now, several years later, with a focus on cozy pieces that inspire a love of adventure and a greater appreciation for my home in the mountains, I've chosen to simplify the shop brand to reflect that. Along with using my own name, simple branding brings the focus back to the love and care that goes into each handmade gift.
Over the years, I have been fortunate enough to send cozy pieces to different parts of the world and keep people fashionably warm or help add a touch of handmade love to their celebrations. I hope I can inspire more adventures, while providing quality and an extra cozy touch.

▼ WILL MY HANDMADE ITEM BE THE SAME COLOR ON SCREEN?
Each item is photographed with care to depict the most accurate color. However, at times actual colors may vary slightly due to different monitor settings, yarn dye lots, etc.
▼ CAN I REQUEST A CUSTOM COLOR, SIZE, ETC THAT IS NOT LISTED?
If you would like a custom item, please contact me & make a request. If I can create your custom item, a special shop listing will be made just for you.
Listed items are already made to sell & therefore are not made to size or customization.
▼ DON'T KNOW IF AN ITEM WILL FIT?
Each item description includes measurements pertaining to fit. You can check your measurements with a seamstress measuring tape or simply use a string measured against a ruler.
Wrap the measuring tape/string around your head, placing it over your ears and through the middle of your forehead to measure your Head Circumference.
Boot Warmers should fit relatively snug around your upper calves. Wrap a measuring tape/string around your upper calf to measure its circumference.
Wrap the measuring tape around the knuckles of your fingers to measure your Hand Circumference.
♦ If an item you love won't fit, you can contact me to request a custom item made to your measurements.
▼ WHY AREN'T YOUR ITEMS MADE OF WOOL?
Unfortunately I am allergic to wool, so handmade accessories are all created with other fibers, like acrylic or cotton. You'd rather have a soft and cozy beanie without any scratchy wool anyway, right?

Ken Januski is an artist living in Philadelphia, PA. All of my recent work focuses on nature, birds in particular. I have exhibited in the annual exhibition of the Society of Wildlife Artists in London in 2011, 2012 ,2015, 2016 and 2018. I just find British and European wildlife art the most appealing.
This store was formerly called berkeleySU, a tip of the hat to the place where I began my printmaking education, the basement of the student union at UC Berkeley. As the store primarily sold my prints when I opened it seemed appropriate. But I have a very lengthy history in abstract art. I also have a fairly old blog called Art, Birds, Nature which seems 
to well summarize my interests. In 2016 I finally decided to try to unify my blog and my Etsy store by using the same name for both. The store now includes work in linocut and woodcut as well as watercolor, acrylic and various drawing media. In 2017 I also began working in moku hanga, a Japanese method of woodblock printing. That is also shown here.
My older strictly abstract work is also available on Etsy at OldAndAbstract.

I started my shop in late 2010 about the same time I took up linocut for the first time ever. Etsy like the perfect place to show and sell this type of multiple-edition work. Eventually I added other types of prints as well as other types of painting and drawing to the shop.
Since 2017 my main printmaking medium has been moku hanga, or Japanese woodblock.
I've been an abstract artist for about 30 years and only turned to naturalism in 2006. My interest in birds, nature and the outdoors became my main artistic subject. Slowly I added media that I used abstractly to my naturalist portfolio. So now I work in watercolor, charcoal, pastel, and acrylic as well as linoleum block, woodblock and moku hanga.
In 2011, 2012, 2015 and 2016 I exhibited in the annual exhibit of the Society of Wildlife Artists in London. In 2011 and 2012 I was a finalist for the BBC Wildlife Artist of the Year in the International Category. I also have exhibited numerous times in the Gallery of the Commons the online gallery of Wildlife Art Journal.

Please use the adjuster slide to open the collar to the full length, then slip it over your dogs head and then pull it up behind the pup’s ears. For walking and training sessions, this is the point where you want to adjust the size of the collar.
You will adjust the collar, by moving the slider once again to make the collar smaller. Pull on the D-ring, and tighten the adjuster loop. The live rings, that do the work, should be at least two inches apart and should never touch.
If they touch, the collar is too loose and your pup will be able to slip out of it. When worn properly, the collar should fit loosely around the middle of the dog’s neck when there is no tension on it.
The Martingale and Half-Check Chain Collars are well suited as part of a positive reinforcement training method and behavior correction method. Both offer more control than a Buckle Collar and offer the trainer the ability to make corrections to behavior as well. The design of the the two loops work in conjunction so that the contraction of the martingale does not choke your dog like a choke chain.
Hand wash in a sink with lukewarm water and a few drops of liquid laundry detergent. Lie on a towel to air dry. Touch up with warm iron.

Vintage clothing is not new so it’s important that you understand the condition of a garment. On some occasions, you will find items that have not been worn which are deadstock or new old stock (NOS). But, for the most part, vintage has been previously worn.
MINT: An item is as perfect and pristine as when it was originally made and shows no sign of wear (mint condition is rare for vintage clothing).
**Please note that Mint Unworn/Deadstock/New Old Stock items may sometimes have storage marks (due to age/elements) on the fabric. This does not constitute as "wear" as the item was never worn.
NEAR MINT: An item shows only the slightest signs of wear.
EXCELLENT: An item shows typical signs of wear due to occasional use.
VERY GOOD: An item is considered wearable but has some surface flaws (staining or soiling, for example).
GOOD: An item is wearable but cannot be returned to excellent condition 
even if repairs are made.
Of course, the older a piece of clothing is, the more likely it will display indications of its age. Signs of wear should be expected. Although condition ranks as a main buying consideration for vintage clothing, it’s not as crucial for older items.
✂ IS MY DRESS CLEAN?
Items are always sent to you in a ready to wear condition. "Estate fresh" garments are never in ready to wear condition so that means we take the extra time/care to either carefully launder and iron our items, steam, press or have them dry cleaned before sending.
The only garments that we do not clean are deadstock/new old stock garments that have not been worn. Collectors prefer these in "Estate fresh" condition. However, if you purchase a deadstock item from us and would prefer it cleaned before sending out, just let us know. There is no charge for this...just request this.
Items are stored with cedar and lavender sachets to keep away moths etc. Please do not purchase if you are allergic to any of those.
If you are also allergic to moth ball odor, "old clothing smell" or "old lady smell", you should not be purchasing vintage...period.
Although we clean every item before listing, vintage clothing has had a life before reaching to us and we cannot be held responsible for your allergic reactions.
Doing a vintage film, play, photo shoot or ad? We may have just what you need. We have special discounts for large orders or on set credits. No rentals though!

This is a very personal painting for me in this series, as this is my own birth month and I feel very connected with her themes of remembrance of the dead.
Every year in Mexico, the monarch butterflies migrate around the time of the Day of the Dead, which has led to the local belief that these are the spirits of the returning deceased there to visit there loved ones every year.
She also channels the Aztec goddess of the dead, Mictēcacihuātl, who is said in one story to have been a sacrifice, herself, before she held dominion over the realm of the dead. This story stuck with me as I painted this piece. The Lady of November acts as a beacon for the dead, guiding them to their loved ones who wait for their promised reunion to celebrate the good memories they hope to keep alive.
"Lady of November" was originally rendered in watercolor and ink and is part of a birthstone series of paintings. Check my other listings to find the other months!

This is a PDF DOWNLOAD to print at home.
This pattern prints on A4 or USA Letter size paper.
If you want a mailed wide format pattern, you can purchase that version in my shop.
This pattern is multi-size 
with waist sizes 22-42" all in the same packet. This is based on a MISSES SIZE pattern. Plus sizes, petites, etc, may need adjustments. PLEASE SEE PHOTOS FOR SIZE CHART.
Evelyn is a beautiful 1910s era skirt that can be made with or without pockets. This skirt hits two inches above the natural waist and falls from the top of an internal fitted waistband. The skirt fastens at the side with hooks and eyes and snaps. The pocket version of the skirt has fold down tabs that attach to a belt. The back of the skirt is gathered. When made without pockets, this works exceptionally well with suit jackets. When paired with a blouse in matching fabric, it makes a wonderful skirt for a two-piece dress.
This pattern is a Wearing History Signature Styles pattern. It was based on an original 1917 sewing pattern, and includes not only the original period sewing instructions, but also modern step-by-step photo instructions and cutting charts for modern fabric widths. This pattern also includes notes about this pattern from Delineator magazines of 1917.
Informative videos about this pattern are coming soon!
Evelyn is shown with the Elsie blouse pattern in our adventure look, and with the 1910s Blouse and Guimpe pattern for the traditional 1910s look. Blouse patterns sold separately. Pair this with our 1916 Suit Pattern for even more 1910s looks!
This pattern is a great option for steampunk, historical, or modern wear!
This pattern is estimated to be an Intermediate pattern difficulty, but adventurous beginner sewers may be able to construct this with a little patience. Our photo instructions make this skirt pattern quite user-friendly!
Because this was based on a period original from an era in which women wore corsets, a mock up is HIGHLY SUGGESTED. Test construction and fit on your unique figure before cutting into your fashion fabric.
YOU WILL NEED ADOBE READER, A FREE PDF READER PROGRAM, IN ORDER TO OPEN AND PRINT THIS PATTERN.

Tell me how Wearing History patterns differ from vintage patterns.
--You do not have to be afraid of harming a delicate original vintage pattern.
--They cost a fraction of the price of purchasing an original rare vintage pattern.
--The patterns are easier to understand and clearly marked pieces instead of holes or dot markings.
--Most patterns are multi-sized so you can cut the size you need. Original vintage patterns were only single size in a packet.
--E-patterns are downloadable and printable at home. You can buy and start sewing in a weekend!
--Several Wearing History patterns are drafted by me and/or have new instructions (These are the Signature Styles patterns).
What sort of fit or ease can I expect with these patterns?
--Very little ease is included in comparison to modern standards, 
and most run true to size.
--Armholes and sleeves fit higher than tighter than modern standards. You may need to alter your sleeves & armscyes if you prefer modern fit with more ease.
--Resto-Vival patterns are based on original period patterns and were meant to be worn with period foundations- Girdles, period bras, etc may make a difference in fit. A Victorian or Edwardian garment will be sized to fit over a corset.
--ALWAYS make a mock up before cutting into your final fabric.
What type of patterns are your "Signature Style" patterns?
New patterns based on original period sources or brand new designs with new step-by-step illustrated instructions, improved fit, and new cutting layouts and yardage requirements for modern fabric widths. These patterns can either be based on period originals with changes that improve the original pattern fit and instructions, or a unique draft to Wearing History that has been drafted by me personally and heavily researched to be period correct. These patterns also include instructions that are hand drawn or digitally drawn and composed by me personally.
What type of patterns are your "Resto-Vival" patterns?
Resto-Vival patterns are restored and revived based on historical pattern source material. Original patterns are usually available only in single sizes, precut from tissue paper and totally unprinted, with details like grainlines and darts indicated only by small perforations. Resto-Vival™ patterns are clearly marked with drawn and labeled markings. Resto-Vival™ patterns follow the period shapes of the original patterns, maintaining the historical accuracy of the completed garment. Original period instructions are included, the complexity of which can vary from pattern to pattern. Older patterns may have text only instructions. Intermediate to advanced sewing knowledge is recommended. We suggest keeping a sewing book handy.
Why do you say to make a mock up? Can't I just cut it out and start sewing?
I ALWAYS suggest to make a muslin mock up to check fit and construction before cutting into your fashion fabric. Every body is different, even if measurements are similar, and making a mock up of inexpensive fabric is the only surefire way to make sure your garment will fit your unique figure and have the ease you want. Don’t make a garment out of your final fabric without testing and expect it to be perfect- it’s just not feasible. It’s kind of like going shopping at the mall– you don’t expect every item on a hanger to fit you perfectly and it requires some trying on. Not all sizes run the same between all the stores and brands. The same is true of sewing patterns, so make your mock up!
Do you offer pattern making or pattern grading services? Do you do custom sewing?
I'm sorry, I do not offer pattern making services, pattern grading services, or custom sewing.
Please view each individual pattern for size information, as size can vary from pattern to pattern.
Please keep in mind that patterns are based on misses or women's sizing. Plus size, juniors, petites, and tall sizes will most likely require additional alterations so I highly suggest making a mock up before sewing your final garment.
Will I receive a diagram I need to draft, or a full size pattern?
All patterns are full size, unless otherwise indicated. They may use a LOT of paper to print, but are already sized and graded for you.
Tell me more about e-patterns. What kind of format are they, and how do I assemble?
When you buy an e-pattern from me, you receive a multi-page PDF file you download to your computer and print at home. The patterns are formatted to fit on both 8.5 x 11 sized letter and A4 paper. All pages are tiled to make it easy for home sewists to print at home and then assemble into a larger pattern sheet.
You print the patterns at 100% scale or "actual size", and then cut and tape the dotted lines together.
All pattern pages are numbered, so you can keep track of you process. An additional file is included to help with assembly- make sure you read it before you print your files.
I have been told by many customers that my e-patterns are some of the easiest to assemble, and I'm thankful for their high praise!

As part of Ontario's 3,200-company, $39 billion agri-food sector, these companies can take advantage of University of Guelph (U of G) research programs that produce partnership and licensing opportunities on innovations like these.
University of Guelph research has resulted in a shortening product that eliminates trans fat and reduces saturated fat in roll-in shortenings used to create laminated doughs in the manufacture of products such as croissants and Danishes. The product features a high liquid oil content and 'beta' crystal structure, yet has high oil-binding capacity and similar mechanical properties as regular 'beta-prime', high solid-fat roll-in 
shortenings.
Soy products are increasingly accepted in western society because of their health benefits and because soy ingredients have good processing functionality. While many companies have made 'cheese' from soy products, these products have not been widely adopted because it is difficult to replicate a texture comparable to natural cheese. University of Guelph researchers have developed a method to mingle milk and soy proteins in the cheese-making process to achieve the health benefits and cost savings of soy with the taste and texture of dairy, with the first proof of concept being a soft ripened cheese product.
"The U of G's Industry Liaison program is the best way for global agri-business companies to access our R&D expertise and resources," said Sue Bennett, Director, University and Community Relations at the University of Guelph. "Working closely with over 800 researchers and 33 academic departments, our Industry Liaison team will quickly find the most appropriate resource and leverage corporate R&D funds at the same time. In fact, provincial and federal Canadian governments that support industry-sponsored research can leverage industry R&D dollars 2:1 or 3:1 and up to 8:1."
The Ontario Food Cluster builds international trade and investment opportunities for its expanding 3,200-company agri-food and beverage sector. Food and beverage processing in the province is expected to grow to a $40 billion industry by end of 2013, and the agriculture and agri-food sector is Ontario's number one employer. TUCSON, AZ -- (MARKET WIRE) -- May 24, 2007 --James Briscoe, CEO of Liberty Star Uranium & Metals Corp. (OTCBB: LBSU), will be featured on Market News First (www.mn1.com) in an exclusive live interview with MN1's Bob Leonard and Rich Hancock. The interview takes place today at 11:30AM EDT. MN1 has written a feature story about LBSU that can be viewed on its website.
Liberty Star Uranium & Metals Corp. is an Arizona-based mineral exploration company engaged in the acquisition and exploration of mineral properties in the states of Arizona and Alaska. Currently we control three properties totaling approximately 160,000 acres (about 250 square miles) which are located over what management considers some of North America's richest mineralized regions for uranium, copper, gold, and molybdenum (moly).
Under our primary North Pipes Super Project, Liberty Star holds 1856 standard Federal lode mining claims covering over 38,000 acres in numerous blocks targeting breccia pipe hosted uranium deposits. The breccia pipes are part of the large uranium bearing breccia pipe terrain which occurs on the Arizona Strip lying just south of the Utah border. Eight mines were brought into production during the 1970s and early 1980s on deposits discovered within the immediate area. The uranium bearing pipes which were mined are the second highest grade uranium mineral deposits in the world and the highest grade in the United States. Previously mined mineralization in these pipes has graded about 0.6% to 0.7% uranium or about 12 to 14 pounds per ton. In addition to uranium they are known to contain copper, zinc, silver, vanadium, cobalt, nickel, molybdenum, gallium, germanium and other metals. Past producers have recovered copper, silver and vanadium as by-products of uranium mining. Liberty Star has a joint venture agreement with XState Resources, Ltd. for exploring, developing, and mining these deposits on an additional 14 claims in Mohave County in Arizona.
Through its wholly owned subsidiary, Big Chunk Corp., Liberty Star also holds the claims to our Big Chunk Super Project, covering approximately 177 square miles in southwestern Alaska and targeting copper, gold and molybdenum; and our Bonanza Hills Project, covering approximately 14 square miles in southwestern Alaska and targeting gold with by-product silver.
Liberty Star Uranium & Metals Corp. was founded in 2004. Formerly known as Liberty Star Gold Corp., in April 2007 we changed our name to Liberty Star Uranium & Metals Corp. to better reflect our current activities.
